name: {{dow}} Cloud Impact Levels
purpose: How sensitive the information is that a cloud service may hold for the {{dow.current}}.
what: Four levels, defined by DISA in section 3.7 of its cloud SRG: IL2 (3.7.1) for public and non-controlled information, IL4 (3.7.2) for CUI and mission data, IL5 (3.7.3) for unclassified national security information, IL6 (3.7.4) for classified up to SECRET.

binds.line: The DFARS lets a cloud contract go only to a provider that DISA has granted a provisional authorization at the level the work needs.

verifiedBy.line: DISA’s authorizing official grants the provisional authorization (3.6). The mission owner’s authorizing official still grants the authorization to operate (section 4).

sits.line: Layer 5. Each level is assessed on a FedRAMP baseline plus the department’s own controls: Moderate or High for IL2 and IL4, High for IL5 and IL6 (3.7.5). The guide does not mention FedRAMP’s new classes.

sources.title: Cloud Service Provider (CSP) Security Requirements Guide (SRG)

verification.note: Read on 24 November 2026 in DISA’s own copy. The document library at https://www.cyber.mil/dccs/dccs-documents/ draws its list by script, so a script sees an empty page; it was opened in a browser, and its Cloud Computing SRG entry, uploaded 26 June 2026, was downloaded as U_Cloud_Computing_Y26M06_SRG.zip. In it, U_Cloud_Service_Provider_V1R7_SRG.pdf prints Version 1, Release 7, 30 June 2026, developed by DISA for the department under its current name. Section 3.7 defines four levels: IL2 for publicly releasable and other nonpublic unclassified information not designated CUI (3.7.1), IL4 for CUI and other mission data (3.7.2), IL5 for nonpublic unclassified national security systems and information, including CUI or mission data whose owner needs more protection than IL4 gives (3.7.3), and IL6 for classified information, at this time only SECRET or below, reached over private SIPRNet connections or approved CNSSP-11 circuits, on infrastructure dedicated and separate from the provider’s other offerings (3.7.4). Section 3.7 also says Impact Levels are a construct of the department only and do not apply to FedRAMP baselines, and that the data of a national security system shall be housed at IL5 or higher. Section 3.7.5 and its Table 3-1 give the FedRAMP baseline each level is assessed on; section 3.6 says the DISA authorizing official approves and revokes provisional authorizations, and section 4 that the mission owner’s authorizing official grants the authorization to operate. The revision history in the same archive dates Release 7 to 30 June 2026, with changes to sections 4.4, 5.5.1 and 5.5.2. The release note of July 2025, below, said CUI was no longer part of IL5; the text of 3.7.3 in Release 7 still lets IL5 take CUI that needs more than IL4. This copy replaces the lead of a vendor page of 10 August 2026, which first named Release 7.

sources.title: Department of Defense Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026. This is the last single-volume guide that could be opened, and it is not the current edition. It gives the four levels in use (level 1 was merged into IL2 and level 3 into IL4), IL2 as non-controlled unclassified information, IL4 as controlled unclassified information, IL6 as classified information up to SECRET, and the provisional authorization as approved by the DISA authorizing official while the mission owner grants the authorization to operate. Read again on 15 November 2026: the archive is still at the same address and still holds Version 1, Release 4 of 14 January 2022.

sources.title: July 2025 Maintenance Release: STIGs to Be Released

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026. For the Cloud Service Provider SRG, Version 1, Release 3: ‘Updated guidance for approach for IL4 addressing both Moderate and High categorizations. IL5 now accommodates unclassified National Security System/National Security Information with CUI no longer part of this Impact Level.’ The guide itself had by then been split into a Cloud Service Provider SRG and mission owner documents. Read again on 15 November 2026: the release note of 2 July 2025 is still at the same address with the same entry for the Cloud Service Provider SRG, Version 1, Release 3.

Read on 14 November 2026: the contracting officer ‘shall only award a contract to acquire cloud computing services from a cloud service provider’ that ‘has been granted provisional authorization by Defense Information Systems Agency, at the level appropriate to the requirement’. The clause DFARS 252.239-7010 carries the guide into the contract. Read again on 15 November 2026: the page still shows the DFARS change of 7 May 2026 and the same paragraph (b)(1).

terms.line: A work of the United States government. Lensatic shows the card only, in its own words, with the guide’s section numbers.

related.line: Each level is assessed on a FedRAMP baseline, though an Impact Level is not a FedRAMP level.
The mission owner’s authorization to operate is an RMF decision.

note: Impact Levels are the department’s own construct and do not apply to FedRAMP baselines, so there is no FedRAMP Impact Level (3.7). Data of a national security system goes in IL5 or higher (3.7); IL5 also takes CUI its owner judges needs more than IL4 (3.7.3). IL6 holds classified information up to SECRET, reached over SIPRNet or approved circuits, on infrastructure kept separate (3.7.4).
